title: The U.S. atomic bombing of Hiroshima on 6 August 1945, and Nagasaki on 9 August
summary: The Department of Energy's Manhattan Project history dates both bombings and Japan's mid-August surrender decision.
body: The U.S. Department of Energy's Manhattan Project history dates the atomic bombing of Hiroshima to 6 August 1945 and the bombing of Nagasaki to 9 August 1945, and it titles a following section "Japan Surrenders, August 10–15, 1945." The instrument of surrender signed on 2 September 1945 is a National Archives document. Casualty figures for the two cities vary by source and by whether later radiation deaths are included; no casualty total was taken from the DOE page's sentences we used, so none is stored. Whether the bombings were militarily necessary, or were also a signal to the Soviet Union, is a historians' argument and is not decided by the dates.

contested_views.label: The dates
contested_views.summary: The DOE history places the two bombings on 6 and 9 August 1945 and Japan's surrender decision in 10–15 August, with the formal instrument on 2 September.

contested_views.label: The decision
contested_views.summary: Historians disagree about whether Japan was about to surrender anyway, what the Soviet declaration of war on 8 August changed, and how to judge the civilian deaths. Those arguments need their own documents. This card does not pick a moral verdict.
